How it works

HOW GEARING SETS YOUR SPEED

Speed = cadence × (chainring ÷ cog) × wheel circumference. A bigger chainring or a smaller cog gives you more speed for each pedal turn; the opposite makes climbing easier.

Development

Development is how far the bike travels for one turn of the pedals, in metres. It's the easiest way to compare gears across different bikes and tyre sizes.

Choosing gears for a climb

On a long climb most riders are happiest at 80–90 rpm. Look at your speed in your easiest gear at 80 rpm and compare it with your speed on the climb (our climb time calculator gives you that). If you'd be grinding below 70 rpm, a bigger cassette or a smaller chainring will help.
